item.title: Aso Adventure & Activity Park — Guide
item.description: Set amid the grasslands and mountains of the Aso region, this outdoor adventure and activity park offers active, family-friendly fun in one of Kumamoto’s most scenic landscapes. Depending on the season and facility, visitors can enjoy attractions such as ziplines and aerial ropeways, obstacle and adventure courses, cycling, water play and splash areas in summer, athletic playgrounds and other hands-on outdoor activities, all set against the sweeping backdrop of the Aso caldera.

item.title: Aso Caldera Farm & Horse Riding — Guide
item.description: The wide, rolling grasslands of the Aso caldera — grazed by cattle and horses for centuries and kept open by traditional burning — are the perfect setting for farm experiences and horse riding. At ranches and farm parks around the caldera, visitors can ride horses across open pasture with the volcanic peaks as a backdrop, take pony rides, feed and meet cows, horses, sheep and other farm animals, and try hands-on activities like milking or butter-making.

item.title: Kumamoto Tea Country — Guide
item.description: The highlands of the Aso region and Kumamoto’s mountains are dotted with beautiful green-tea plantations, where neat rows of tea bushes carpet the rolling hills in vivid green. Kumamoto produces well-regarded Japanese green tea, and its cool, misty upland climate and volcanic soils are ideal for cultivating it. In tea-growing villages, visitors can take in the scenic terraced fields, especially lovely in the fresh green of the new-leaf season in late spring, learn about tea cultivation and processing, and — depending on the spot — sample or buy fresh local tea, enjoy tea-flavoured sweets, or join seasonal tea-picking experiences.

item.title: Ujitawara Gorge — Guide
item.description: Ujitawara Gorge, in the mountainous Aso region of Kumamoto, is a scenic river gorge offering a cool and refreshing escape into nature. Clear mountain waters flow through a valley of rock formations, pools and greenery, with waterfalls tumbling amid the forest and shaded walking paths following the stream. In the warmer months it’s a wonderfully cooling spot, the water and tree canopy keeping the air fresh even in summer, and in autumn the surrounding maples and foliage turn the gorge into a tapestry of colour.
